Hi TAG,

This is an FYI about Chromium's planned implementation of the existing SVG2 side attribute on <textPath>.

During the Intent to Ship discussion, Blink API owners recommended notifying the TAG for awareness. We have already sent the Intent to Ship; apologies for the late notification. This issue is intended as an FYI rather than a request for a full design review, but feedback is welcome.

Feature summary

The side attribute controls which side of a path the text is placed on. Setting side="right" effectively reverses the path direction for text layout.

This allows authors to place text on the inside or outside of a shape, such as a circular path, without duplicating or manually reversing the path data.

Specification

  • SVG2 definition:
    https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/text.html#TextPathElementSideAttribute
  • Related SVG Working Group discussion about the IDL:
    w3c/svgwg#1086

Implementation references

  • Chromium:
    https://issues.chromium.org/issues/40362379
  • Firefox:
    https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2034371
  • WebKit:
    WebKit/WebKit#66616

Chromium shipping plans

We are targeting Chrome 156, subject to the remaining shipping approvals.

  • ChromeStatus:
    https://chromestatus.com/feature/5422782593761280
  • Intent to Ship discussion:
    https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/d/msgid/blink-dev/6aab4606.edf999b6.27416f.0002.GAE%40google.com

Thanks!

items.content_html:
Ask your question.
Architectural issue (not a spec review): user-agency failure in OS/web workspace sync connectors.

Asks for TAG

  1. Treat automatic remapping of well-known local directories as an architecture/user-agency issue where web and workspace connectors participate.
  2. Record a principle: local file operations must not depend on remote quota or connectivity; an empty remote account must not be allowed to overwrite or dehydrate a larger local tree without an explicit, reversible, step-by-step consent that states the direction of sync and the billing consequence.
  3. Recommend a mandatory “hard severance” that restores independent local paths without leftover placeholders.

items.content_html:
The Media Working Group maintains registries related to some of its specifications on the Recommendation track, namely Media Source Extensions (MSE), Encrypted Media Extensions (EME) and WebCodecs. The registries are published on the Registry Track as Registry Drafts. The Media Working Group would like to advance these documents on the Registry Track by publishing them as Candidate Registry Snapshot.

We're taking the liberty to request a review of all the registries at once and without further analysis because the registries all have similar registration entry requirements, and because it isn't clear to us what input you might be willing to receive to help your review of such documents. By definition, registries document values, they do not define any architectural or interoperability requirements related to those values. We would expect comments on these requirements to be raised against the underlying specifications (MSE, EME, WebCodecs).

You may raise issues that apply to all registries using the tracking issue at w3c/media-wg#64. More specific issues may be raised in the repositories that hold the documents.

Registry linked to MSE (GitHub repo):

  • Media Source Extensions Byte Stream Format Registry

Registries linked to EME (GitHub repo):

  • Encrypted Media Extensions Initialization Data Format Registry
  • Encrypted Media Extensions Stream Format Registry
  • Encrypted Media Extensions HDCP Version Registry

Registries linked to WebCodecs (GitHub repo):

  • WebCodecs Codec Registry
  • WebCodecs VideoFrame Metadata Registry

Note: Most of the registries related to MSE and EME used to be published on the Note track (simply because the Registry track did not exist at the time of publication).

Track conversations at https://tag-github-bot.w3.org/gh/w3ctag/design-reviews/1268

  • What do the end-users experience with this proposal: End users experience synchronized, frame-accurate captions and translated subtitles during media playback and live conferencing, interactive "click-to-seek" transcript navigation, and seamless alignment between speech transcripts and recorded media tracks.
  • User research you did to validate the problem and/or design, if any: Live conferencing / media synchronization studies and interactive validation demos:
    • Live Meeting Caption Sync & Recording Demo: https://alan33d.github.io/web-speech-demos/live_meeting_recording_demo.html

  • This work is being funded by: Google

  • Multi-stakeholder feedback:
    • Chromium comments: Positive / In active development (https://chromestatus.com/feature/5811907077472256)
    • Mozilla comments: Active discussion in WebAudio/web-speech-api#191 and WebAudio/web-speech-api#192 (comment) by @padenot (provided guidance on using double in seconds, non-nullable attributes, and naming speechStartTime/speechEndTime to mirror speechstart/speechend).
    • WebKit comments: Standards position to be filed at https://github.com/WebKit/standards-positions/
  • Major unresolved issues with or opposition to this specification: None. Consensus reached on using non-nullable double representing seconds relative to audio stream start, named speechStartTime and speechEndTime.
  • Status/issue trackers for implementations:
    • Chrome Status: https://chromestatus.com/feature/5811907077472256
    • Chromium Issue Tracker: https://issues.chromium.org/issues/528037568

You should also know that...

W3C Audio WG/CG Meeting Discussion: This feature was presented and discussed during the W3C Audio WG/CG Teleconference on August 13, 2026 (see Meeting Minutes). The group aligned on developer needs for media timeline association (e.g. generating VTTCue captions, click-to-seek transcripts, and synchronizing captions with recorded video).

  • Mozilla's feedback in PRs was also discussed and addressed during the meeting.
  • Interactive demonstrations showcasing subtitle synchronization, recording timeline alignment, and the inadequacy of existing coarse DOM event timestamps were presented at the WG meeting and are available for testing:
    • https://alan33d.github.io/web-speech-demos/live_meeting_recording_demo.html
    • https://alan33d.github.io/web-speech-demos/webrtc_caption_sync_test.html

The specification

  • Follows the Web Platform Design Principles.
  • Includes Security and Privacy Considerations sections based on answers to the Security/Privacy Questionnaire.

Where and by whom is the work is being done?

  • GitHub repo: https://github.com/w3c/gpc
  • Primary contacts:
    • Nick Doty (@npdoty), Center for Democracy and Technology, Privacy Working Group Chair
    • Christine Runnegar, Privacy Working Group Chair, Invited Expert
    • Peter Snyder (@pes10k), Brave, Privacy Working Group Chair and GPC Spec Editor
    • Sebastian Zimmeck (@SebastianZimmeck), Wesleyan University, GPC Spec Editor
    • Justin Brookman (@j-br0), Consumer Reports, GPC Spec Editor
    • Aram Zucker-Scharff (@AramZS), The Washington Post, GPC Spec Editor
  • Organization/project driving the specification: GPC group with contributors from:
    • Academia (e.g., Wesleyan University)
    • Civil society organizations (e.g., Consumer Reports and Center for Democracy and Technology)
    • Browser vendors (e.g., Brave, DuckDuckGo, and Mozilla)
    • Web publishers (e.g., The Washington Post and Digital Content Next)
    • Tech companies (e.g., Google)
    • And other web stakeholders ...
  • This work is being funded by:
    • National Science Foundation
      • #2618248 SaTC 2.0: RES: Enforcing Privacy Opt-out Compliance for a Trustworthy Web
      • #2055196 SaTC: CORE: Small: Improving Internet Privacy with Global Privacy Control
    • Alfred P. Sloan Foundation Grant under the Program for Universal Access to Knowledge
    • Wesleyan University
      • Grants in Support of Scholarship
      • Anil Fernando Endowment
  • Primary standards group developing this feature: Privacy Working Group
  • Incubation and standards groups that have discussed the design:
    • Privacy Working Group, Minutes

Feedback so far

  • Active horizontal reviews: TBD
  • Multi-stakeholder feedback:
    • Chromium comments: TBD
    • Mozilla comments: TBD https://github.com/mozilla/standards-positions/issues/NNN
    • WebKit comments: TBD https://github.com/WebKit/standards-positions/issues/NNN
    • Feedback/review from developers, implementers, civil society, and others}}
      • A usability survey found that 94% of the participants would turn on GPC and 81% showed a correct understanding of what GPC does ensuring that their intent is accurately represented by their choice.
  • Major unresolved issues with or opposition to this specification: None
  • Status/issue trackers for implementations:
    • Chrome status: TBD
    • Firefox status: Mozilla Support Global Privacy Control
    • Safari status: Apple Developer Documentation globalPrivacyControlEnabled
    • Brave status: Brave Help Center How do I change my Privacy Settings?
    • DuckDuckGo status: Global Privacy Control (GPC) Enabled by Default in DuckDuckGo Apps & Extensions

You should also know that...

  • As of August 14, 2026, 385,000+ websites declare compliance with GPC as indicated via the GPC .well-known support resource
  • Per Amazon's Additional State-Specific Privacy Disclosures, "In 2025, Amazon received approximately 349.5 million cross-context behavioral advertising opt-out requests. The large majority of those requests are from visits to our website with GPC already enabled."
  • GPC is required by law in at least five US states: California, Connecticut, Colorado, Oregon, and New Jersey. It is actively enforced. See, e.g., Connecticut, California and Colorado Announce Joint Investigative Privacy Sweep.
  • Starting on January 1, 2027 every browser is required to have a GPC setting under the California Opt Me Out Act, an amendment to the California Consumer Privacy Act.
  • Under its proposed amendment of the General Data Protection Regulation with privacy preference signals in a new Art. 88b under the European Union's Digital Omnibus, the European Commission expressed interest to adopt GPC.
  • Research showed that "enabling the Global Privacy Control (GPC) signal initially reduces the number of intractable cookies by 30% on average, with a further 32% reduction possible on subsequent visits by rejecting the banners."

  • An introduction to the feature, aimed at unfamiliar audiences: https://w3c.github.io/vc-barcodes/#introduction
  • A description of the problems that end-users were facing before this proposal:https://w3c.github.io/vc-barcodes/#introduction (existing optical barcodes on security critical documents are often unprotected and trivially forged; there is no compact, non-proprietary way to prove authenticity, integrity and status of the printed data)
  • Alternatives considered: Non-CBOR serializations of Verifiable Credentials were considered, but are incompatibly large with standard barcode size constraints.
  • Examples of how to use the proposal to solve the end-users' problems: https://w3c.github.io/vc-barcodes/#test-vectors, https://w3c.github.io/vc-barcodes/#introductory-examples
  • What do the end-users experience with this proposal: a verifier optically scans a barcode with trusted software and learns whether the data is authentic, unmodified, and (optionally) not revoked/suspended.
  • User research you did to validate the problem and/or design, if any: Feedback and extensive discussion from production deployments (CA DMV) and pilot programs (DHS, US First Responders, US Vital Records)
  • Test Suite: N/A, will be created when transitioning into CR, expectations will be to follow existing pattern for VC test suites at https://w3c.github.io/vc-data-integrity/implementations/#test-suite-reports resulting in additions to the VC ecosystem conformance dashboard: https://canivc.com/

NOTE: The VCWG has volunteered to follow the new Threat Modelling approach championed by the Security IG, which largely replaces the traditional Security/Privacy Considerations section with a new Threat Model section: https://w3c.github.io/vc-barcodes/#threat-model and a more comprehensive Threat Model document: https://w3c.github.io/vc-barcodes/threat-model/
